mainEntity.name: When do I need a construction project manager for my residential project?

acceptedAnswer.text: You typically need a construction project manager when your residential project is complex, involves multiple subcontractors, or has a tight budget and timeline. This could include new home construction, significant remodels, or additions. A project manager ensures all trades are coordinated, permits are secured, and materials are ordered efficiently. Their expertise helps prevent delays, cost overruns, and quality issues, providing a single point of contact for all project-related communications.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider a construction project manager for complex residential projects, large remodels, or new builds to ensure coordination, budget adherence, and timely completion.
